issue.title: Harden R4G1 inference hot path: remove recursion/panic fallbacks and broaden zero-allocation kernel coverage

Addressed both review points in the latest commit:

1. Added fixed-capacity `visited` sets (independent of stack contents) in both iterative traversals in `engine.rs` to guarantee termination on cyclic child graphs.
2. Replaced the limited-operand `saturating_mul_small` implementation with a shift/add saturating multiply that is correct for all `i32` inputs without using multiplication operators.

Validation run after changes: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, plus the graph-format no-default-feature checks.

reviews.body:
## Pull request overview This PR hardens the R4G1 runtime inference hot path toward the recursion-free, panic-free, allocation-free contract by converting recursive traversals to bounded iterative walks, removing `unreachable!` fallbacks from transformerless prediction, extending zero-allocation census coverage across more kernels, and removing multiplication operators from the runtime Cayley–Dickson scoring path. **Changes:** - Replaced recursive node traversal helpers in `uor-r4-graph-runtime` with fixed-capacity explicit stacks and added a bound when iterating nodes from caller-provided buffers. - Replaced `unreachable!` panic fallbacks in transformerless prediction with a safe fallback path and added an empty-store test. - Expanded allocation census to measure `predict_token`, `predict_distribution`, `predict_candidates`, and `step` together using caller-owned fixed buffers. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | crates/uor-r4-graph-runtime/src/engine.rs | Converts recursive graph traversal helpers to iterative, fixed-capacity stack-based traversal; bounds candidate scanning by `min(node_count, node_scores.len())`. | | crates/uor-r4-graph-runtime/src/cayley_dickson.rs | Removes multiplication usage in hashing and scalar product via shift/add helpers. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/runtime.rs | Replaces panic-based “level 0 always populated” assumptions with a safe fallback prediction path. | | crates/uor-r4-core/tests/{allocation_census.rs,window_paths.rs} | Extends allocation census to more kernels and adds an empty-store non-panicking regression test. |
Comments suppressed due to low confidence (1) **crates/uor-r4-graph-runtime/src/engine.rs:433** * `collect_target_leaf_nodes` has the same cycle issue as the updated `check_node_emits`: it prevents duplicates only among nodes currently on the stack. In the presence of cyclic child edges (especially among nodes with `emission_len == 0`, which are never recorded in `out`), this loop can run forever because nodes can be popped and then pushed again later. Please add a bounded fixed-capacity visited set (independent from `out`) to guarantee termination. ``` if let Some(edge) = base_graph.edge((start + i) as u32) { let dst = edge.dst.0; if stack_len < stack.len() && !stack[..stack_len].contains(&dst) { stack[stack_len] = dst; stack_len += 1; ```

review_comments.body:
The new iterative traversal only de-duplicates nodes that are currently on the stack (`!stack[..stack_len].contains(&dst)`). If the graph contains a cycle (e.g. A→B→A), a node can be popped and then re-pushed later, leading to an infinite loop in `check_node_emits` (unbounded runtime on adversarial graph shapes). This needs a bounded, fixed-capacity "visited" set (or other cycle break) in addition to the stack check.

This issue also appears on line 429 of the same file.

`saturating_mul_small` returns `0` for any `rhs` outside { -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 }. Since `CayleyDicksonVector.coords` is `pub`, callers can construct vectors with arbitrary coordinate values, and `endomorphism_scalar_product` would silently compute an incorrect scalar product in those cases. If the intent is to keep the function correct for all `i32` without using multiplication, implement a shift/add-based saturating multiply fallback (or make the invariant explicit by constraining the type/fields).
